P0-4.core-entity.observed_scope: Logical actor identity survives projection replacement and unload/reload in the actor lifecycle service.
P0-4.core-entity.uncovered_scope: No live Minecraft entity spawn/despawn, client projection, or multi-world runtime fixture.

P0-4.display.observed_scope: JVM render-model tests cover custom/default texture selection, name visibility, and name/title formatting.
P0-4.display.uncovered_scope: No live client render, resource reload, skin download, or GUI resolution fixture.

P0-4.combat.observed_scope: NpcDefinitionSerdeTest verifies authored maxHealth 50.0, attackDamage 8.5, and movementSpeed 0.28 survive JSON serialization round-trip.
P0-4.combat.uncovered_scope: No numeric-bound validation, server combat damage, melee/ranged behavior, resistance or immunity, defeat/respawn, XP/drop, or live server fixture.

P0-4.inventory.observed_scope: Serde tests cover slotted inventory with item components and legacy string-list migration onto visible drop slots; NpcInventoryTest covers the slot layout contract, bounded stacks/components, equip/unequip without loss, and drop index/chance bounds.
P0-4.inventory.uncovered_scope: No live inventory GUI/session, persistence reload of equipped state on a live server, or target-runtime inventory fixture.

P0-4.ai.observed_scope: Unit tests cover waypoint LOOP/PING_PONG transitions, stuck-detector recovery/stop behavior; P3-3 policy tests cover bounded targeting policy data, deterministic relationship fallback, and threat target-change reasons.
P0-4.ai.uncovered_scope: No live entity navigation, wander-radius, path-work budget, or large-population performance fixture.

P0-4.targeting.observed_scope: Threat-manager tests cover retaliation target acquisition and threat-decay target clearing.
P0-4.targeting.uncovered_scope: No faction-policy targeting, entity defeat lifecycle, or server-world combat fixture.

P0-4.dialogue-definition.observed_scope: JVM tests cover valid dialogue YAML loading, dialogue YAML writer round-trip, graph JSON field round-trip, and service save with source-index refresh. P5-1 validator tests cover unreachable-node/dangling-edge errors and legal-cycle warnings.
P0-4.dialogue-definition.uncovered_scope: No live editor-screen authoring, client/server synchronization, or rendered dialogue fixture.

P0-4.dialogue-choice.observed_scope: Application-service tests cover conditional graph choice actions, invalid option indexes, and close-dialogue actions; P5-2 protocol tests cover opaque server-issued tokens bound to actor/dialogue/session/revision, exactly-once consumption, index/unknown/stale-token rejection, expiry, and session revocation.
P0-4.dialogue-choice.uncovered_scope: No live packet-to-service choice fixture, concurrent-choice determinism on a live server, or target-runtime choice fixture.

P0-4.quest-definition.observed_scope: JVM tests cover valid quest YAML loading, circular prerequisite rejection, writer-to-filesystem-to-loader round-trip of namespaced ID, title, description, category, DAILY repeat, prerequisite, two objective type/target/count values, and two reward type/target/amount values; namespace-collision and sanitized-path-collision preservation; loader-indexed reuse of pre-upgrade or renamed files; duplicate-ID saves and deletes fail closed without overwriting or removing source files; malformed-candidate fail-closed behavior; unrelated malformed YAML isolation; rejection of path traversal; concurrent same-definition saves serialized by a shared lifecycle-owned coordinator and cooperating-process file lock with unique atomic temporary files; deletion of a legacy flat-root quest clears its source index and permits recreation; failed YAML deletion leaves the quest registered with unchanged revision and a rejected canonical delete; and concurrent application-service save/delete leaves registry, source index, and reloaded YAML in agreement.
P0-4.quest-definition.uncovered_scope: Not every RepeatType, QuestObjective.Type, or QuestReward.Type enum value is round-tripped; corrupt unparseable legacy files require manual recovery; external file renames made after load require reloading definitions before save; concurrent same-ID writes are serialized but last-writer-wins; symlink escape coverage is skipped when the Windows test account cannot create symbolic links; a hostile local process can race path validation and rename unless the definitions root remains admin-controlled; no live quest editor, client/server synchronization, or Minecraft runtime fixture.

P0-4.quest-completion.observed_scope: Application-service tests cover progression/reward completion, duplicate reward prevention, invalid-reward preflight, mark-before-deliver exactly-once XP delivery across failed commit and restart, crash-after-mark no-redelivery, mark-failure aborts before delivery, and login-time recovery resuming interrupted fan-out exactly once; P5-5 tests cover durable mail overflow, once-only claiming, and team progression surviving member changes.
P0-4.quest-completion.uncovered_scope: No process-kill/live-server recovery fixture beyond headless crash-injection and no target-runtime completion fixture.

P0-4.quest-progression.observed_scope: Typed start/progress mutations are scoped to a player, checked against that player's persisted quest revision, payload-bound for request-ID retries during one process lifetime, rejected as stale after restart, protected by actor/subject authorization, and rolled back in memory when the durable write fails; completion advances the persisted revision and automatic completion returns its final revision; per-player event groups preserve commit order under reentrant and concurrent mutations, and listener registration during delivery does not strand the queue; objective counts at 100,000 are accepted and higher counts rejected; objective-threshold auto-completion remains active; concurrent in-process quest turn-ins apply faction rewards once. P2-3 added mark-before-deliver durable reward legs with login-time recovery of interrupted fan-out.
P0-4.quest-progression.uncovered_scope: Quest reward fan-out across a real process kill is exercised only by headless crash-injection fixtures; remaining operation families beyond quest/faction/follower/bank/trade route through typed requests but lack live-server fixtures; target runtime behavior remains unverified.
